newsitem.title: USA: US Sugar delays harvest ahead of Florida tax vote.
newsitem.headline: US Sugar delays harvest ahead of Florida tax vote.

text.p: TALLAHASSEE, Fla, Oct. 25 (Reuter) U.S. Sugar Corp is postponing its sugar harvest by at least one week to allow employees to fan out to convince Florida voters to scuttle a proposed penny-a-pound tax on sugar to pay for Everglades cleanup.

Nearly 2,500 full-time U.S. Sugar employees will be given the option next week to stay away from work and canvas cities to speak out against the tax, said company spokeswoman Judy Sanchez. Employees will be paid their normal weekly wages.
"This is a tax on the growers," Sanchez said. "The other side says it will be paid for at grocery stores but that is not the case."

The last-minute drive is expected to make the city of Clewiston a virtually ghost town as sugar employees leave to fight the tax. The lobbying is voluntary, but Sanchez said she expects a lot of employees to participate.
"This is very much an agricultural community," Sanchez said. "There are many similar towns down here that rely on the industry."
The exodus will postpone the sugar harvest until after the U.S. general election, Sanchez said. The delay could be costly to growers if the weather turns bad or cold temperatures arrive.

Florida voters on November 5 will decide whether a one cent-per pound tax will be levied on sugar produced in South Florida. Tax proceeds will be deposited in a trust fund to pay for restoration of the Everglades, the fabled "River of Grass" that supporters of the tax say has been decimated by sugar farming.
Sugar growers say they are only partly to blame for Everglades damage and are already paying their fair share.
"There are 5.5 million more people down here than when the Everglades ran free," Sanchez said. "About 3.5 million are living on former Everglades land."
